problem: No leaf anywhere covers content management. 'Add a blog', 'let a non-developer edit the marketing site' and 'where do docs and help articles live' are among the most frequent web tasks, yet the tree has no CMS, MDX or content-model leaf. growth-marketing covers what to write, not where content lives or how it is previewed and published.
fix: Add two leaves to react-nextjs > rendering-strategies.md (8 -> 10 leaves): 'Choose where content lives: repo MDX, a headless CMS or a site builder' (core) and 'Model content types and wire draft preview and publish-time revalidation' (pro). Add a useWhen entry 'Add a blog, docs or CMS so non-developers can edit pages' (9 -> 10) and extend the file purpose with 'or where editable content lives'.

problem: Data residency is named in four leaves (cloud-infrastructure platform-choice, privacy-compliance privacy-law, ai-features ai-data-privacy, and here) but no leaf teaches how to build it: a second regional stack, tenant-to-region routing, what stays global. The only engineering leaf is the three-in-one expert leaf 'Support per-tenant configuration, custom domains and data residency', which is also the only place that serving customer custom domains appears. The first EU or enterprise customer who asks where their data lives hits exactly this.
fix: Replace that leaf with three in the same file (8 -> 10 leaves): 'Pin each tenant to a home region with isolated regional stacks and global routing' (expert); 'Serve customer custom domains with ownership verification and on-demand TLS certificates' (expert); 'Support per-tenant settings and limits without forking the codebase' (pro). No overlap with web-security 'Sandbox user-supplied code, HTML and custom domains', which is the security side.

problem: Selling to the first customer in another country triggers sanctions and export-control duties (blocked countries and parties, screening, what the payment provider does and does not cover). Nothing in the tree mentions sanctions or export controls; privacy, VAT and consumer law are covered but this is not.
fix: Add to privacy-compliance > sector-consumer-rules.md (8 -> 9 leaves): 'Block sanctioned countries and parties and check export-control rules before selling abroad' (pro).

problem: The first enterprise, regulated or public-sector buyer commonly asks to run the product in their own cloud or on-premises. The tree covers SSO, SCIM, audit logs, DPA, SOC 2, SLA and 'Move a large tenant to dedicated infrastructure', but has no leaf for deciding whether to offer self-hosted or customer-cloud deployment and what supporting it costs. It is a hard-to-reverse fork that founders usually make under deal pressure.
fix: Add to engineering-leadership > technical-strategy.md (7 -> 8 leaves): 'Decide whether to offer self-hosted or customer-cloud deployments and price their upkeep' (expert).

problem: The file purpose promises 'selling, merging or shutting down', but the only shutdown leaf is product-level ('Sunset a product gracefully with notice, refunds and customer data export'). Winding down the company itself (creditors, staff, customers, dissolution, final filings) is the most common way a startup ends and has no leaf.
fix: Add to startup-finance > exit-due-diligence.md (9 -> 10 leaves): 'Wind down the company: settle debts, notify customers and staff, dissolve, file final returns' (pro). Add a useWhen entry 'We are out of runway; how do I shut the company down properly?' (9 -> 10).

problem: A co-founder split is covered only before it happens ('Choose a co-founder and sign a roles, vesting and decision-rights agreement', 'Raise co-founder disagreements early and resolve them') and on the equity mechanics ('Handle a departure: repurchase, exercise window and acceleration' in startup-finance). The separation itself has no leaf: the agreement and release, board seat, handover of accounts and access, and what to tell team, customers and investors.
fix: Add to company-building > founder-effectiveness.md (8 -> 9 leaves): 'Negotiate a co-founder exit: separation agreement, board seat, access handover and announcement' (expert).

problem: A competitor copying the product, or a clone or phishing site using the brand, has no leaf. The tree registers a trademark and handles takedown notices received, but never enforces the founder's own rights, never decides how to respond to a fast follower, and never mentions patents or trade secrets.
fix: Add to company-building > strategy-moats.md (7 -> 8 leaves): 'Respond to a copycat: ignore, out-ship, reposition or enforce your rights' (pro). Add to company-building > incorporation-founders.md (8 -> 10 leaves): 'Enforce trademark and copyright against clones with takedowns and platform complaints' (pro) and 'Decide whether patents or trade-secret protection are worth their cost' (expert).

problem: The mobile branch covers the web-versus-native decision, wrappers, store review, in-app purchase and staged rollouts, but not the two things that eat the first weeks of a real app: links that open the installed app (needed for magic-link sign-in, password reset and sharing), and automated builds, signing and store submission. pwa-mobile.md is at the 10-leaf cap and frontend-foundations at the 8-reference cap, so nothing can simply be appended.
fix: In frontend-foundations > pwa-mobile.md replace 'Handle offline storage and sync conflicts on devices' (expert, already owned by backend-architecture > realtime.md 'Build collaborative or offline-first features with a sync engine or CRDTs') with 'Open emailed and shared URLs in the installed app with universal and app links' (pro). Add to ci-cd-release > ci-pipelines.md (7 -> 8 leaves): 'Automate mobile builds, code signing, store submission and over-the-air updates' (expert).

problem: Cryptography appears only as individual uses (Argon2id passwords, webhook signatures, hashed reset tokens, field encryption) plus 'never hand-roll crypto'. No leaf teaches choosing the right primitive for a job, which is where application code goes wrong: non-random tokens, unauthenticated encryption, a hash where a MAC is needed, wrong JWT algorithm.
fix: Add to web-security > secrets.md (8 -> 9 leaves): 'Pick the right primitive: random tokens, hashes, HMAC, authenticated encryption or signatures' (core). Extend the file purpose with 'or choosing a cryptographic primitive'.

problem: The tree chooses a backend language and runtime, an API style and a frontend meta-framework, but never answers the question this reader asks first: is the Next.js server my backend, or do I need a separate API service, and on which framework? No leaf names a backend framework decision at all.
fix: Add to backend-architecture > architecture-shape.md (9 -> 10 leaves): 'Choose between the meta-framework's server and a separate API service with its own framework' (core).

problem: When users abuse the product (phishing pages, spam, malware links), the consequence that actually takes the business offline is external: an abuse notice from the cloud host or registrar with a short deadline, or a browser deceptive-site warning on the whole domain. Email blocklisting and DMCA/DSA notices are covered; these are not.
fix: Add to auth-identity > abuse-defense.md (9 -> 10 leaves): 'Answer host, registrar and browser-blocklist abuse notices before they suspend you' (pro).

problem: First deploy has per-domain pre-launch leaves (security baseline checklist, bug bash, status page, marketing launch checklist) but no operational go-live gate that checks backups are restore-tested, alerts reach a phone, rollback works and limits are set. The file also has no core leaf, so the roadmap shows nothing to do here before launch.
fix: Add to site-reliability > postmortems-runbooks.md (7 -> 8 leaves): 'Run a production-readiness review before launch: backups, alerts, rollback, limits and owners' (core). Extend the file purpose with 'or before a launch'.

problem: Paid custom work has no leaf. An enterprise customer who will sign 'if you build X', paid implementation or migration, and consulting to fund the product early are all common, and all need scope, change control, acceptance and a services price. The tree covers proposals, pilots and MSAs but not a statement of work or services pricing. This also covers the reading of the request in which 'customers' are clients of a web developer.
fix: Add to sales-customers > proposals-contracts.md (8 -> 10 leaves): 'Scope custom work in a statement of work with change control and acceptance' (pro) and 'Price services as fixed bid, day rate or retainer without subsidizing the customer' (pro).

problem: The skill's useWhen promises 'Do I need Redis, Elasticsearch, a vector database or Kafka for this?', but the decision leaf lists only 'Redis, a search engine, object storage or a vector index'. Queues and streams are a coverage-floor item, and the tree goes from 'Start with a Postgres-backed queue and know when to outgrow it' straight to expert stream design with no leaf deciding whether a broker or log is needed.
fix: Add to data-stores > choosing-datastores.md (8 -> 9 leaves): 'Decide when a job queue must give way to a broker or event log' (pro).

problem: 'Let someone go lawfully and humanely' is the only leaf for a first firing and is marked expert (specialist depth, needed at scale). A founder can need it with the first hire, so it disappears from the roadmap exactly when it is needed.
fix: Change the level of 'Let someone go lawfully and humanely' from expert to pro in company-building > managing-people.md.

where: build.py and every skills/*.json (order of skills inside a layer)
problem: build.py orders skills inside a layer by file name (sorted glob), so tree.md teaches data-stores ('when a product needs more than Postgres') before postgres-database, 3dui before frontend-foundations, ai-features before backend-architecture and api-design, product-analytics before product-discovery, ci-cd-release before cloud-infrastructure, accessibility before ui-ux-design, and ai-coding-agents before git-collaboration and code-quality. A learner reading top to bottom meets the specialist branch before its foundation.
fix: Add an integer "order" field to each skill JSON and change the sort key in build.py to (layer, s.get('order', 99), order[name]). Values: L2 cloud-infrastructure 1, ci-cd-release 2. L3 postgres-database 1, data-stores 2. L4 backend-architecture 1, api-design 2, email-notifications 3, payments-billing 4, ai-features 5. L5 auth-identity 1, web-security 2, privacy-compliance 3. L6 frontend-foundations 1, react-nextjs 2, 3dui 3. L7 ui-ux-design 1, accessibility 2. L8 git-collaboration 1, code-quality 2, ai-coding-agents 3, engineering-leadership 4. L10 product-discovery 1, product-analytics 2. Layers 0, 1, 9, 11, 12 keep their current order. Inside linux-server, move shell-files.md to be the first reference (shell basics before the USE method).

problem: 'Lock down our AWS account' has two obvious owners. web-security useWhen says 'Harden our cloud, admin panel and staff accounts before launch' and owns 'Enforce MFA and least privilege on cloud, registrar, repository and SaaS accounts' and 'Scan infrastructure code and cloud configuration for misconfigurations'. cloud-infrastructure useWhen says 'Set up AWS, GCP or Azure accounts, IAM roles and permissions properly' and owns 'Secure the cloud root account...', 'Grant least-privilege IAM roles...' and 'Audit unused permissions and publicly exposed resources...'. web-security has no notFor pointing at cloud-infrastructure (all 6 slots are used) and cloud-infrastructure only points back for secrets.
fix: Remove cloud from web-security instead of adding a notFor: (1) useWhen becomes 'Harden our admin panel, staff accounts and SaaS logins before launch'. (2) Reword the leaf to 'Enforce MFA and least privilege on registrar, repository, payment and SaaS accounts' (core). (3) Move 'Scan infrastructure code and cloud configuration for misconfigurations' (pro) to cloud-infrastructure > infrastructure-as-code.md. (4) Retitle the reference 'Hardening company accounts, staff access and admin tools'. (5) In cloud-infrastructure, change the notFor topic 'Storing and rotating secrets' to 'Secrets, staff SSO and devices, and admin-panel hardening' (use: web-security).

problem: useWhen 'What tech stack should I choose for this product?' and the reference purpose 'Read when choosing a stack' promise stack selection, but no leaf teaches it (closest is 'Choose boring, well-supported technology...'). The pieces are claimed separately by react-nextjs ('Which framework...'), backend-architecture ('Which backend language or runtime...'), cloud-infrastructure ('Where should I host this...') and postgres-database ('ORM or raw SQL, UUIDs or integer IDs'), so the most common greenfield question has four partial owners and no whole one.
fix: Add leaf 'Pick a full default stack for a new product, with each choice's flip condition' (core) to engineering-leadership > technical-strategy.md. Reword the useWhen to 'What whole tech stack should I start this product on?'. Widen the notFor topic 'Designing a specific system's modules and services' to 'Choosing a backend runtime or designing a system's modules and services' (use: backend-architecture). The notFor list is full, so the single-layer questions stay disambiguated by the existing useWhen wording in react-nextjs, backend-architecture and cloud-infrastructure.

where: ui-ux-design, growth-marketing, sales-customers, email-notifications (useWhen) and growth-marketing > landing-conversion.md
problem: 'Onboarding' is a trigger in three skills with no notFor between ui-ux-design and sales-customers or from growth-marketing to ui-ux-design: 'Design the flow for onboarding, settings or a new feature' (ui-ux-design), 'Write the onboarding and lifecycle email sequence' (growth-marketing), 'Onboard a new business customer successfully' (sales-customers). 'Welcome email' is also claimed twice (email-notifications useWhen and growth-marketing leaf 'Write a welcome and activation sequence...'). And growth-marketing leaf 'Cut signup friction: remove every optional step before first value' repeats ui-ux-design leaf 'Cut a flow's steps, decisions and fields to the minimum'.
fix: Reword the triggers so each names its own facet: ui-ux-design 'Design the in-app flow for first run, settings or a new feature before I build it'; growth-marketing 'Write the welcome, activation and win-back email sequence'; sales-customers 'Run kickoff, data import and training for a newly signed business customer'; email-notifications 'Send a receipt, verification or password-reset email from the app'. Delete the growth-marketing leaf 'Cut signup friction: remove every optional step before first value' (landing-conversion.md drops to 6 leaves).

problem: 'Add an AI support chatbot' is obvious for both: sales-customers useWhen 'Set up customer support: inbox, help center and an AI support agent' with leaf 'Deploy an AI support agent grounded in docs with human escalation', and ai-features useWhen 'Add an AI assistant, chat or summarization feature' plus retrieval.md and guardrails.md. Neither points at the other and both notFor lists are full. The same skill also takes an engineering build request, 'Build an internal admin tool so support can fix things themselves', while holding one leaf on it.
fix: Keep the build in ai-features and the policy in sales-customers. useWhen becomes 'Set up customer support: inbox, help center, response targets and escalation'. Reword the leaf to 'Decide what an AI support agent may answer and when it hands off to a human' (pro). Reword the admin-tool useWhen to 'Decide what an internal admin tool must let support do without an engineer'.

where: company-building > strategy-moats.md; accessibility > names-roles-aria.md; product-analytics > north-star-metrics.md; ui-ux-design > dark-mode-theming.md
problem: Four leaves contradict their own skill's notFor. (a) company-building leaf 'Choose a market and problem worth years of your life' versus its notFor 'Choosing which problem and customer to pursue => product-discovery'. (b) accessibility leaf 'Make data tables and charts understandable without sight' versus notFor 'Accessible charts and data-visualization design => dataviz'. (c) product-analytics leaf 'Build one dashboard the company reviews every week' versus notFor 'Running the analysis: SQL queries, statistics and dashboards from data => data'. (d) ui-ux-design leaf 'Let users choose system, light or dark and persist it without a flash' is CSS and script implementation, versus notFor 'Implementing layout, theming and animation in CSS => frontend-foundations'; it is also marked core, and no product needs a theme switcher to ship.
fix: (a) Delete the company-building leaf; product-discovery > problem-validation.md already has 'Score ideas on pain, payer clarity, reachability and founder advantage'. (b) Reword to 'Make data tables understandable without sight: headers, scope and captions' (pro). (c) Reword to 'Choose the handful of numbers the company reviews every week' (core). (d) Reword the ui-ux-design leaf to 'Decide whether to offer a theme switcher and default to the system setting' (pro), and reword frontend-foundations > css-layout.md 'Implement theming with color-scheme, light-dark() and OKLCH custom properties' to 'Implement themes with color-scheme, light-dark() and OKLCH custom properties, without a load flash' (pro).

problem: Deciding whether to use Kubernetes is expert ('Decide whether Kubernetes is justified over a managed platform') but operating it is pro: 'Operate Kubernetes deployments, probes, rollouts and config', 'Debug a pod stuck Pending, crash-looping or failing readiness', 'Set resource requests and limits and configure pod autoscaling'. Pro means needed to run in production with paying customers, and the house default is Kubernetes only with people to run it. The expert decision leaf also repeats the core leaf 'Decide between a PaaS, managed containers, a VPS and Kubernetes for your stage'.
fix: Set all three pro leaves in kubernetes.md to expert, so the whole reference is expert. Delete 'Decide whether Kubernetes is justified over a managed platform' from platform-choice.md (the core leaf owns the decision).

where: linux-server (hardware-resources.md, processes-systemd.md, shell-files.md, packages-updates.md, ssh-hardening.md, time-encoding.md) and web-networking (tls-certificates.md, proxies-load-balancers.md)
problem: Twelve leaves that only matter when you run your own host are marked core ('needed to ship a real product at all'), against the house default of a PaaS first. It is also inconsistent inside the plan: 'Deploy containers to one VPS with Kamal or Coolify' and 'Provision a server repeatably...' are pro, yet setting up that VPS is core. The roadmap would tell a founder on a PaaS that writing systemd units is a prerequisite to shipping.
fix: Change core to pro for: 'Write a systemd unit that restarts on crash and starts on boot'; 'Set log rotation, disk alerts and swap policy before a host fills'; 'Transfer and sync files with rsync and scp, preserving permissions'; 'Install and pin packages with apt or dnf from trusted repositories'; 'Apply kernel and package security updates on a schedule, including reboots'; 'Audit what is installed, running and listening before exposing a host'; 'Set up a fresh VPS: non-root user, sudo, firewall and updates'; 'Harden SSH: keys only, no root login, restricted users'; 'Configure a host firewall that allows only the ports in use'; 'Run servers in UTC and keep clocks synced with NTP'; web-networking 'Configure TLS 1.3 and disable legacy protocols and ciphers'; web-networking 'Configure a reverse proxy with routing, timeouts, compression and forwarded headers'. linux-server keeps 17 core leaves (reading resources, processes and logs, shell, SSH keys, containers, UTC and UTF-8).

where: linux-server > time-encoding.md; site-reliability > capacity-scaling.md; git-collaboration > versioning-releases.md; data-stores > caching-redis.md; cloud-infrastructure > infrastructure-as-code.md; ai-features > retrieval.md; api-design > webhooks.md; growth-marketing > content-marketing.md
problem: Eight single-leaf level errors. Too low for what they are: tenant leaks through RAG and SSRF through customer webhook URLs are launch-blocking wherever the feature exists, and zone names are a precondition of the pro DST leaf. Too high: the others are marked core but depend on a pro practice or are not needed to ship.
fix: 'Store time-zone names, not offsets, and keep the zone database current': expert to pro. 'Enforce per-user and per-tenant permissions inside retrieval': pro to core (matches data-stores 'Enforce tenant and permission filters inside every search query', core). 'Deliver outbound webhooks without letting customer URLs reach internal networks': expert to pro (same level as 'Send signed webhooks...'). 'Run two or more instances behind a health-checked load balancer': core to pro. 'Apply semantic versioning to libraries and APIs': core to pro. 'Measure hit rate and prove a cache earns its complexity': core to pro (adding the cache is pro). 'Read a plan diff and catch a destructive change before applying': core to pro (using Terraform is pro). 'Build in public with consistent founder-led content': core to pro.

where: backend-architecture > runtime-language.md; web-networking > tls-certificates.md; api-design > api-style.md; frontend-foundations > javascript-typescript.md; privacy-compliance > sector-consumer-rules.md
problem: Six leaves a 2026 practitioner would correct. (a) 'Prefer runtime built-ins (fetch, test runner, watch) over extra dependencies' contradicts the WRITING.md house default of Vitest. (b) 'Configure TLS 1.3 and disable legacy protocols and ciphers' reads as TLS 1.3 only; production still needs a 1.2 fallback. (c) 'Enable HSTS and preload after verifying every subdomain' presents preload, which is slow to undo, as a core step. (d) 'Describe REST APIs in OpenAPI 3.1...' pins a version; 3.2 has been published (writer to verify) and the number will keep aging. (e) 'Use modern built-ins (structuredClone, Intl, Temporal, iterators)...' names Temporal unconditionally while the same skill says to target Baseline; Temporal was not in every engine at my last check (writer to verify). (f) 'Meet EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability-reporting and update duties' assumes the Act applies; it covers products with digital elements placed on the market, not hosted SaaS as such.
fix: (a) 'Prefer runtime built-ins (fetch, crypto, watch mode, env files) over extra dependencies'. (b) 'Serve TLS 1.3 with a TLS 1.2 fallback and disable everything older'. (c) 'Enable HSTS with a staged max-age; preload only once every subdomain serves HTTPS'. (d) 'Describe REST APIs in OpenAPI and generate typed clients'. (e) 'Use Baseline built-ins (structuredClone, Intl, iterator helpers, Temporal when Baseline) instead of libraries'. (f) 'Decide whether the EU Cyber Resilience Act covers software you distribute, and meet its duties'.

problem: 'Decide build versus buy for auth, payments, email, search and analytics' (core) is five decisions in one leaf, and each is already owned by its domain skill: auth-identity 'Decide between a managed auth provider and a vetted library', payments-billing 'Choose a payment provider or merchant of record', email-notifications 'Choose an email provider...', data-stores 'Choose a search engine...', product-analytics 'Choose an analytics tool...'. It makes engineering-leadership a second obvious answer to 'Should I use Clerk or build auth?'.
fix: Reword to the method the domain skills do not own: 'Decide build versus buy from differentiation, yearly ownership cost and exit path' (core).

problem: Three duplicate pairs inside one skill. (a) 'Route payments to a secondary processor for uptime and acceptance' (checkout-integration.md, expert) and 'Keep a second processor and portable payment tokens ready' (refunds-disputes-fraud.md, expert). (b) 'Choose a payment provider or merchant of record for your markets' (checkout-integration.md, core) and 'Decide between a merchant of record and handling sales tax and VAT yourself' (invoices-tax.md, core). (c) 'Resolve an unknown outcome after a timeout by querying, never re-charging' (checkout-integration.md, pro) and 'Recover the payment state after a lost response, reload or closed tab' (checkout-experience.md, pro).
fix: (a) Delete the refunds-disputes-fraud.md leaf and reword the checkout-integration.md one to 'Add a second processor with portable payment tokens for uptime and freeze risk' (expert). (b) Reword the checkout-integration.md leaf to 'Choose a payment provider by markets, payment methods, fees and payout terms' (core); the merchant-of-record decision stays in invoices-tax.md. (c) Delete the checkout-experience.md leaf (drops to 6 leaves).
